title: Projective representability of the full Hilbert functor by Hilbert polynomial
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian), and let $E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, put $E_T=E\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $\operatorname{Hilb}_{E/S}(T)$ be the set of closed subschemes $Z\subset E_T$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] over $T$. Pullback makes this a functor, represented by a scheme $H=\coprod_P H_P$. The index is the numerical Hilbert polynomial of each geometric fibre with respect to the specified projective embedding: the polynomial eventually equal to the dimension of the degree-$m$ part of its homogeneous coordinate ring. Each $H_P\to S$ is H-projective [def-kun-projective], hence separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $H_P$ represents the subfunctor with fibre Hilbert polynomial $P$ everywhere. The universal closed subscheme in $E\times_SH$ and this identification commute with arbitrary base change. No flatness of $E\to S$ is assumed. The empty subscheme is allowed.

source.place: Grothendieck, Bourbaki Expose 221, Theorems 3.1--3.2 and the Hilbert specialization following Proposition 3.8, printed pp.259--266; Remark 3.9, p.266, reduction to projective space. Modern finitely presented version on all test schemes; original simplifies to locally Noetherian test schemes. Archival PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Pullback preserves the closed immersion, flatness, and finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The fibre-product identity for two consecutive pullbacks gives the functor laws. By [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality], the fibre polynomial is well defined, unchanged by residue-field extension, and locally constant on every test scheme. Consequently $T=\coprod_P T_P$, where $T_P$ is the open and closed locus with polynomial $P$. It suffices to represent the constant-$P$ functor. Keep $P=0$ throughout; it is the empty-subscheme functor.

source.place: Theorem 3.1, decomposition preceding Theorem 3.2; finitely presented version on all test schemes

proof.text: Choose one $m\geq1$ for $(n,P)$ from [lem-sfb-hilbert-uniform-section-bound]. If $P(d)$ is negative or nonintegral for some $d\geq m$, or $P(m)>\binom{n+m}{n}$, its rank conclusions exclude every family on a nonempty test scheme; the empty scheme represents this component and is H-projective. Otherwise [lem-sfb-bounded-hilbert-grassmann-chart] gives, on every affine $U\subset S$, a finite-type immersion $Y_U\to G_U$ representing the constant-$P$ families. Here $G=G_S(\binom{n+m}{n},P(m))$ is H-projective by [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective]. All the maps to $G$ classify the same degree-$m$ restriction quotient, so agree on open restrictions.

source.place: Theorem 2.1 and Lemmas 3.3--3.4; bounded Grassmannian charts

proof.text: For every DVR $R$ over $S$, [lem-sfb-projective-dvr-flat-closure] extends each generic closed family uniquely over $R$, preserving its fibre polynomial $P$. Apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-chart-gluing-projectivity] to the charts of step 2 and these unique lifts. It gives $H_P$, its universal closed family, and its H-projectivity, separatedness and finite type over $S$.

source.place: Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 3.7: gluing, DVR extension and projectivity

proof.text: Set $H=\coprod_PH_P$ and take the disjoint union of their universal closed families in $E_H=\coprod_PE_{H_P}$. A family on $T$ has the canonical open-and-closed decomposition $T=\coprod_PT_P$ from [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality]; on $T_P$ it gives the unique classifying map to $H_P$, and these maps glue to $T\to H$. Conversely the inverse images of the components under $T\to H$ recover those pieces and their families. This proves representability of the full functor, allowing nonconstant fibre polynomials on disconnected bases. Finally for any $S'\to S$ and any $S'$-scheme $T$, the identification $(E\times_SS')\times_{S'}T=E\times_ST$ identifies its families and their pullbacks exactly. Hence $H\times_SS'$ and its pulled-back universal family represent the base-changed functor, with pieces $H_P\times_SS'$. The natural bijections already constructed give this identification; [lem-pc-representable-unique] makes it canonical. The zero-polynomial piece is $S$, since each of its geometric fibres must be empty by [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality], and a scheme with every fibre empty is empty.

source.place: Theorem 3.1, Hilbert specialization after Proposition 3.8, Remark 3.9; arbitrary base change by the represented functor
